gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: The ___ cost was much higher than the estimate.
gaps.explanation: 'Actual' means real or existing in fact; 'current' means belonging to the present time.

gaps.sentence: Many people fell asleep ___ the lecture.
gaps.hint: within the period of an event
gaps.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun (the lecture) and means within that time; 'while' needs a clause with a verb.

gaps.sentence: The two designs are quite ___ from each other.
gaps.explanation: 'Different from' — the adjective is required after 'quite'.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.
'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.
